question: Which drug does EANO call the most important single agent?

options.E: Intrathecal cytarabine as the only drug

explanation: High-dose intravenous methotrexate is described as the most important and beneficial single agent [1].
sourceArticle: EANO guidelines for primary CNS lymphoma in immunocompetent patients, with a section on immunosuppressed patients

question: What consolidation did this update strengthen?

options.A: Autologous stem-cell transplant in first-line treatment
options.B: Routine full-dose whole-brain radiotherapy for every patient

correctAnswerText: Autologous stem-cell transplant in first-line treatment
explanation: A main change is strengthened evidence for consolidation with autologous stem-cell transplant in the first line [1].
sourceArticle: EANO guidelines for primary CNS lymphoma in immunocompetent patients, with a section on immunosuppressed patients

question: How does the guideline describe rituximab?

options.B: It is mandatory in every regimen
options.E: It cures intraocular disease by itself

explanation: The update says the role of rituximab still needs clarification and the data remain inconclusive [1].
sourceArticle: EANO guidelines for primary CNS lymphoma in immunocompetent patients, with a section on immunosuppressed patients

question: Reduced-dose whole-brain radiotherapy of 23.4–30 Gy in complete responders is:

options.A: An option still being tested in randomised trials
options.B: The required standard for every patient
options.D: Given as a single 30 Gy fraction

correctAnswerText: An option still being tested in randomised trials
explanation: Reduced-dose whole-brain radiotherapy, 23.4–30 Gy, in patients in complete response is a therapeutic option currently being investigated in randomised trials [1].
sourceArticle: EANO guidelines for primary CNS lymphoma in immunocompetent patients, with a section on immunosuppressed patients

question: Why is the methotrexate dose not quoted as a single number?

options.A: The guideline says the optimal dose has not been determined
options.E: Dose does not affect CNS penetration

correctAnswerText: The guideline says the optimal dose has not been determined
explanation: Penetration depends on total dose and infusion rate, and the optimal dose has not been determined [1].
sourceArticle: EANO guidelines for primary CNS lymphoma in immunocompetent patients, with a section on immunosuppressed patients
